sections.description: Adds a new bullet to the adverse economic trends list disclosing uncertain global trade policies and related government actions, including tariffs, as a risk to consumer and business spending and stakeholder relationships.

A.rationale: criterion 1 and 2: a new risk (trade policy and tariff uncertainty) is disclosed; the remaining changes are page-footer movement only.

B.rationale: criterion 1: a new risk (trade policy and tariff uncertainty) is disclosed; the page footer changes are ignorable.

sections.description: The share of revenue generated from activities outside the U.S. changes from approximately 70% during 2024 to approximately 71% during 2025.

A.rationale: criterion 4: a share-of-revenue percentage changes (70% to 71%), which goes beyond the year roll-forward.

B.rationale: criterion 4: a share-of-revenue figure changes (70% to 71%) beyond the routine year roll-forward.

sections.description: Adds a sentence that Mastercard or its customers could take, or be perceived to take, actions related to high-risk merchant industries (adult content, firearms, alcohol, tobacco) that could be viewed negatively and result in threats or other retaliatory actions.

A.rationale: criterion 1: a new exposure (threats or retaliation arising from Mastercard's or customers' own actions toward these industries) is disclosed.

B.rationale: criterion 1: a new exposure (threats and retaliation over actions toward these industries) is disclosed.

sections.description: The ESG risk now says disclosures, statements and metrics could be viewed as "inaccurate or unlawful" (previously only "inaccurate"), and rewords the workplace initiative from "equal opportunities for all of our employees" to "where everyone has the opportunity to succeed" and drops "equitably" from digital economy participation.

A.rationale: criterion 3: scope widened by adding the possibility that ESG disclosures are viewed as unlawful, a new legal exposure beyond inaccuracy; the other rewording and footer changes alone would be minor.

B.rationale: criterion 3: scope widened by adding the possibility that the company's own ESG statements are viewed as unlawful, a new legal exposure (also criterion 1); the initiative rewording alone would be stylistic.

sections.description: The talent risk narrows the competitive skill-set market from "technology and other areas that are important to the growth of our business" to "emerging technologies", drops the discussion of employees' different career motivations (project-based or gig work versus linear careers), and removes "our ability to innovate" from the listed impacts of failing to meet workforce expectations.

A.rationale: criterion 1 and 3: previously disclosed exposures (gig-style career motivations, impact on ability to innovate) are removed and the scope of the talent competition risk is narrowed.

B.rationale: criterion 1: previously disclosed exposures (gig/project-based career motivations and harm to ability to innovate) are removed, and criterion 3: scope of the talent-competition risk is narrowed.

sections.description: The inherited litigation risk from acquisitions no longer says it may "impact our ability to successfully finance that business", keeping only the increase in post-acquisition costs of operations.

A.rationale: criterion 1: a previously disclosed exposure (impairment of the ability to finance an acquired business) is removed.

B.rationale: criterion 1: a previously disclosed consequence of inherited litigation (financing impairment) is removed, narrowing scope under criterion 3; the page footer deletion is ignorable.

sections.description: The guarantor risk now cites that Brazil recently enacted regulation requiring PSOs in Brazil (including Mastercard and Visa) to extend responsibility for the financial and settlement integrity of payments to merchants, says more jurisdictions may enact similar approaches with impact on cost of operations and financial condition, and drops the U.S. qualifier on recent bank failures.

A.rationale: criterion 2 and 3: a new specific regulation and jurisdiction (Brazil) is referenced, the hypothetical extension of guarantee obligations becomes realized, and severity widens to include financial condition.

B.rationale: criterion 2: a new specific regulation and jurisdiction (Brazil PSO settlement-integrity rule) is referenced, and criterion 3: the guarantee-extension risk moves from hypothetical to realized.

sections.description: Mastercard Foundation's stated share of general voting power changes from approximately 9.4% as of December 31, 2024 to "greater than 5%" with no as-of date.

A.rationale: criterion 4: a disclosed ownership percentage changes (approximately 9.4% to greater than 5%), reflecting continued share sales under the diversification plan.

B.rationale: criterion 4: the disclosed ownership percentage changes from a point figure of approximately 9.4% to a threshold of greater than 5%.
